title: Ouroboros
description: A continuous single-line serpent wrapped around the inner forearm — the eternal loop drawn in fine, deliberate strokes. Designed to follow the movement of the wrist, the piece stays elegant at rest and catches every turn of the hand.
designNotes: The ring was drawn freehand on skin first, then committed in a single uninterrupted line. Scale work was kept intentionally light so the negative space stays as important as the ink.

title: Feral Crown
description: A geometric fox locked inside a decorative crown of line and dotwork. Bold black fills do the heavy lifting, while the surrounding negative space keeps the piece balanced rather than heavy.
designNotes: Built on a strict grid, the piece uses only two line weights — a discipline that gives the whole composition its sharp, confident rhythm.

title: Sovereign Gaze
description: A hyper-detailed macro study of a feline eye, rendered in soft grey realism. The iris was built from dozens of micro-tones to give the piece genuine depth — the kind of tattoo that reads as a photograph from across the room.
designNotes: Worked in short, tight strokes around the curve of the shoulder so the realism follows the body rather than fighting it.

title: Iron & Bloom
description: A dagger driven through a full-bloom rose — classic traditional flash reworked with cleaner lines and a wider color story. Heavy outlines, honest color, built to last.
designNotes: The palette was limited to five colors on purpose. Traditional works best when it commits to a story and tells it simply.

title: Tide Walker
description: A koi moving against a current of teal and vermillion. The scale work is packed and saturated, built layer by layer until the fish looks like it is pushing through water, not resting on skin.
designNotes: The water behind the koi was packed first, then the fish was drawn into the remaining space — a backwards method that keeps the centerpiece the star.

title: Idle Line
description: A single continuous line tracing a profile — one breath of a line for the whole face. No shading, no second stroke. Just the confidence to stop when the drawing is done.
designNotes: The whole gesture is a study in restraint: the line never crosses itself, and the negative space carries the image as much as the ink.

title: Ember Veil
description: An old, muddied piece retired under a deep ornamental mandala. Dark, layered fill and negative-space line work turned an unwanted tattoo into the anchor of a full back composition.
designNotes: Cover-ups are architecture. The new design had to sit darker than the old ink at every point, with enough texture to make the transition invisible.

title: Prism Lotus
description: A geometric lotus refracted through a violet prism of color fills and clean line work. Sacred geometry with a modern, saturated finish.
designNotes: Each petal received its own gradient pass, so the whole piece reads like light moving through glass on top of the ribcage.

title: Osseous
description: A bone-white ornamental skull drawn from pure geometry — circles, wedges and negative space instead of shading. Medical illustration meets blackwork.
designNotes: The piece uses dead-black fills only where they earn their place, letting the bone structure glow against the skin.

title: Static Bloom
description: A single stem drawn in fine line work from collarbone to sternum, ending in a quiet bloom. No fill, no color — just drawing, placed where the body gives it depth.
designNotes: The stem follows the natural line of the collarbone so the piece feels like it grew there.

title: Ledger
description: A fully custom navigational piece, drawn from scratch around the client's coordinates and route. Compass geometry, custom text and a measured grid that means something only to the person wearing it.
designNotes: Built from seven fine-line layers of decreasing opacity — a depth effect that reads like an old chart.

title: Cardinal
description: A hardened swallow in navy and amber, drafted in the traditional style with confident anchors and a proper outline. The kind of tattoo that outlives trends.
designNotes: The wing feathers were kept bold enough to read clearly from across a room — traditional rules, applied properly.

title: Solstice
description: A single feather floating in negative space, drawn with realism-weight shading that gives the barbs individual life. Simple subject, serious drawing.
designNotes: Shading was worked in the direction of the feather's curve, which makes the piece catch light like the real thing.

title: Minutiae
description: Three small geometric forms strung along the ankle — a line, an arc and a dot. Barely ink, exactly deliberate.
designNotes: The piece was placed after walking the client through three positions, so the marks land exactly where they feel right.

title: Rekindled
description: A blackwork flame folded into a repeating ornamental shape. The symmetry is broken exactly once, on purpose — that break is the piece.
designNotes: Drawn on a six-foot axis and mirrored; the single deliberate break in the pattern gives the eye a place to land.

title: Petrichor
description: Layers of fine-line wave tracing down the outer arm, with a single bird carved into the negative space between two swells.
designNotes: The wave lines were tapered to zero at their ends, so the piece dissolves into clean skin instead of stopping abruptly.

title: Vessel
description: A geometric stag rendered in full-back realism — faceted, exact and unmistakably personal. The largest project in the studio’s portfolio, built over five sessions and one year of drawing.
designNotes: Drawn as a set of interlocking geometric planes, a decision that lets soft realism shading live inside a hard architectural frame.
